Ideally, DHPs could be installed to cool both common areas, at the ends of the hallways, and in upstairs corner units that complain about abnormally high temperatures (three units). DHPs can also be used for heating in the shoulder seasons, but if the building manager wishes to do so, it is advisable to investigate the performance of the specific DHP installed to determine the range of outdoor temperatures where it can operate cost-effectively. Having a second heating system, even one that may not be cost-effective to operate year-round, will give the building some added resilience.
